newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN MINERALS MINISTER MULLS BLACK OWNERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN MINERALS MINISTER MULLS BLACK OWNERSHIP.

text.p: Newly-appointed Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna on Tuesday urged legislators to be "realistic" in their search for ways in which to increase black involvement in the economy.
He told the parliamentary mineral and energy affairs committees that he was examining various ways in which black ownership of mineral rights could be increased.

But this did not involve, as suggested by one legislator, appeals to mining houses to donate mineral rights to the state for redistribution to blacks, who have historically worked in, but not owned, mines.
"The issue of mineral rights pains me, knowing as I do that we are one of only two countries where mineral right are owned by entities other than the state," Maduna said.

"But I have learnt to be realistic in this matter and accept that business people are not in business for altruistic reasons. I can't see Harry or Nicky (Oppenheimer) walking into my office with a briefcase full of documents which I have to sign as deeds of donation."
The state also did not have the money to buy mineral rights from private companies and Maduna rejected the suggestion that nationalisation might be an option.
